title: Distributional Analysis
description: Reveal who wins and loses under a model by breaking outcomes down across income deciles, age cohorts, regions and household types, with honest, uncertainty-aware visualisations.
rationale: Aggregate fiscal numbers hide the politics of policy. Distributional analysis answers 'what does this mean for me and people like me?' and materially improves fairness/poverty scoring and research depth.
success_criteria: A model's outcomes are broken down across all four dimensions
Distributional results are visualised clearly with uncertainty shown
Breakdowns are sourced/caveated and consistent with aggregate totals
Fairness / Poverty scores can optionally incorporate distribution
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Income deciles
- Age cohorts
- Regional impacts
- Household types
- Distribution visualisations

## Out of scope
- The underlying channel modelling (EPIC-012)
- Monte Carlo over distributions (EPIC-014)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-012 - credible breakdowns require the advanced engine's channels
- EPIC-001 - base fiscal aggregates to distribute

## Assumptions
- Suitable distributional reference data is available and citable
- Breakdowns are modelled approximations, clearly caveated
- Visualisations are honest about uncertainty (carried from EPIC-012)

## Risks
- Distributional data poor/unavailable -> source carefully; document; degrade
- Misuse to claim precise personal impact -> frame as group-level approximations
- Visual complexity overwhelms -> clear, progressive visualisations
- Combinatorial explosion -> precompute common cuts; lazy-load detail

## Future extensions
- Intersectional breakdowns (e.g. region x decile)
- Personal 'impact estimator' (heavily caveated)
- Time-evolving distributional paths across the horizon
